topic.title: Bandit Regret and Uncertainty-Driven Exploration
topic.overview: Bandit algorithms choose actions while learning their rewards, balancing immediate value against information that improves later choices. This cluster studies structured and contextual models, Thompson sampling, implicit exploration, and high-probability regret. It asks how much exploration is necessary and how uncertainty should influence action selection.
topic.whyItMatters: Forcing uniform exploration can waste effort on poor actions, but insufficient exploration can lock a learner into a mistake. Strong guarantees help distinguish efficient uncertainty management from lucky performance on a particular reward sequence.
topic.evolution: Early representatives develop Gaussian-process, linear, and generalized-linear bandits. Later work sharpens exploration and posterior-sampling guarantees across structured settings. Recent analyses study variance-aware policies, safety–inference tradeoffs, and an optimization interpretation of Thompson sampling in which residual uncertainty regularizes greedy behavior.
openQuestions: How can posterior-sampling methods remain reliable when their model is misspecified?
What tradeoff is unavoidable between low regret and accurate statistical inference about rarely chosen actions?
